newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares follow France up, set to track US.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares follow France up, set to track US.

text.p: Danish share prices closed higher on Monday after early falls on the left-wing victory in France's elections, echoing later French and European advances, with dealers seeing the market tracking Wall Street on Tuesday.

"The French market had discounted the Socialist election victory and closed higher and this rubbed off on us and the rest of Europe, fuelling gains. Wall Street will determine the way Danish shares go tomorrow," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index finished 1.07 point up at 164.84 while the KFX June future rose 1.65 point to 166.05 with 1,047 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Most of the day's main activity was centred on non-index paper.
But Carlsberg put on 10 crowns to end at 395 on the eve of the announcement of what analysts expect to be a 9.6 percent better first-half 1996/97 result than in the previous year.
Overall turnover for the day was 1.154 billion crowns. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
